result: Improved numerical values for the Wichmann-Kroll contribution to the Lamb shift are obtained for a wide range of nuclear charges, with a discrepancy found for Li-like ions compared to previous work.
conclusion: The calculations reduce theoretical uncertainties and can be extended to related two-loop QED diagrams.

title: Peak-Decomposition-Free Inverse Metrology Of Hyperspectral Moir\'e Photoluminescence
authors: Katsunori Wakabayashi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperspectral photoluminescence (PL) of moir\'e transition-metal dichalcogenide heterobilayers encodes spatially varying exciton landscapes, but extracting that information is hampered by the ambiguity of multi-peak spectral decomposition. Here we develop a peak-decomposition-free inverse framework for quantitative optical metrology of effective disorder coordinates. From the raw cube [MATH] we construct physically motivated descriptor maps -- centroid energy, dominant emission energy, spectral width, low/high spectral-weight ratio, and dominant--centroid offset. Their spatial autocorrelation hierarchy and covariance structure form a robust descriptor fingerprint of multi-scale disorder-sensitive spectral statistics. By matching these descriptor summary statistics to a minimal smooth-plus-trap generative model through a grid-Bayesian inverse, we infer effective disorder coordinates [MATH] with explicit uncertainties. Using synthetic PL cubes generated from controlled multi-scale landscapes, we recover the well-identified smooth-disorder coordinates and constrain the trap sector up to a strength--density degeneracy. We report this degeneracy explicitly as an intrinsic identifiability limit rather than a deficiency of the method, and map four canonical disorder regimes onto a disorder-coordinate diagram. The descriptor statistics are stable against shot noise and pixel pitch, and behave predictably under optical-resolution and energy-window changes. The same pipeline ingests experimental cubes without modification, making it directly applicable to two-dimensional and moir\'e materials. Our results establish descriptor-based hyperspectral PL as a practical, minimal-assumption route to optical disorder diagnostics and provide the validated core of a reusable analysis workflow () for moir\'e exciton systems.
tldr: This paper develops a peak-decomposition-free inverse metrology framework for hyperspectral photoluminescence of moiré TMD heterobilayers to infer disorder coordinates.
motivation: Extracting spatially varying exciton landscapes from hyperspectral PL is hampered by the ambiguity of multi-peak spectral decomposition.
method: The authors construct physically motivated descriptor maps from raw spectral cubes and match their summary statistics to a generative model via grid-Bayesian inversion.
result: The method recovers smooth-disorder coordinates and identifies a strength-density degeneracy in the trap sector, mapping four disorder regimes onto a coordinate diagram.
conclusion: Descriptor-based hyperspectral PL provides a practical, minimal-assumption route to optical disorder diagnostics for moiré exciton systems.

title: Cyclic Codes Over A Commutative Non-unitary Ring Of Order 4
authors: Jon-Lark Kim Marvin Olavides
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the commutative non-unitary ring of order [MATH] arising in the classification of Fine. In this paper, we investigate cyclic codes over [MATH] through their associated residue and torsion codes over [MATH]. We introduce the notions of twisted and untwisted cyclic codes and characterize cyclicity in terms of a compatibility condition involving the twist map and the cyclic shift. Connections between cyclic codes over [MATH] and binary quasi-cyclic codes are established via Gray maps. In particular, we show that the Gray image of a cyclic code over [MATH] is a binary quasi-cyclic code of index [MATH]. We also study duality properties of cyclic codes over [MATH] and prove that the dual of a cyclic code is again cyclic. Finally, we classify permutation inequivalent cyclic codes over [MATH] for lengths [MATH] and determine various structural properties of these codes.
tldr: This paper studies cyclic codes over a commutative non-unitary ring of order 4, focusing on algebraic coding theory without quantum information or thermodynamics connections.
motivation: To understand the structure and properties of cyclic codes over a specific non-unitary ring, extending classical coding theory.
method: The authors define twisted and untwisted cyclic codes, characterize cyclicity via a compatibility condition, and use Gray maps to relate codes over the ring to binary quasi-cyclic codes.
result: They establish that the Gray image of a cyclic code over the ring is a binary quasi-cyclic code, prove duality properties, and classify permutation inequivalent cyclic codes for small lengths.
conclusion: The work contributes to algebraic coding theory but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: The Certification Limits Of KS-Type Layer Relaxations: A Square-Root Ceiling And Its Breakdown
authors: Guillaume Lecomte
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A separable bilinear layer relaxation assigns a population cost to each layer and a nonpositive bilinear coupling to each pair of layers, then excludes a profile span whenever the relaxed minimum exceeds a reference value. We ask what a Kuznetsov-Sahinidis-type relaxation can certify at best. Let gamma = g(1) be the singleton-layer cost. For every valid relaxation with gamma > -1/2, every reference bounded per particle, and every underlying system satisfying two elementary low-energy witness conditions, we prove that the certified deficit N - rho(N) is at most of order sqrt(N), with an explicit bound depending only on the reference bound and gamma. Thus no relaxation in this class can certify a larger asymptotic deficit, independently of the detailed layer cost, interaction kernel, or reference. The threshold is sharp in the abstract witness class: at gamma = -1/2 we construct a valid relaxation with a bounded sound reference and deficit N - 1. The geometric Lennard-Jones system behaves differently. A three-atom chain restores the square-root ceiling at the endpoint, while sufficiently negative singleton costs allow valid relaxations with linear deficit. For still lower costs, beyond the stability constant, no sound relaxation excludes any span. These regimes define a certification spectrum for layer relaxations and reveal a reentrant transition between no exclusion, linear exclusion, and the universal square-root ceiling.
tldr: This paper studies certification limits of a specific class of layer relaxations, proving a square-root ceiling on the certified deficit and showing exceptions for certain systems.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limitations of Kuznetsov-Sahinidis-type layer relaxations in certifying properties of complex systems.
method: The author defines a class of separable bilinear layer relaxations and proves upper bounds on the certified deficit using low-energy witness conditions, then constructs counterexamples for specific parameter regimes.
result: For valid relaxations with singleton-layer cost gamma > -1/2, the certified deficit is at most O(sqrt(N)), with a sharp threshold at gamma = -1/2 where linear deficit becomes possible, and a reentrant transition in the Lennard-Jones system.
conclusion: The certification power of these relaxations is fundamentally limited by a square-root ceiling, except in special cases where linear exclusion or no exclusion occurs.

title: Generalized Segmented Grand For Guesswork Reduction In Turbo Product Decoding
authors: Lukas Rapp, Jiewei Feng, Muriel M\'edard, Ken R. Duffy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Guessing random additive noise decoding (GRAND) can efficiently decode any moderately redundant code with near maximum likelihood (ML) performance via noise effect guessing. For binary linear codes, Rowshan and Yuan's Segmented GRAND was the first to show that constrained guessing can reduce guesswork. Although powerful, their approach requires a specific parity-check matrix structure that limits the number of constraints that can be exploited as well as the class of applicable codes. Here we introduce GSegGRAND, a generalization of Segmented GRAND that circumvents its limitations. Built on a novel parity check structure and a transformation that maps codes into this structure, GSegGRAND efficiently incorporates up to log2(n) constraints for a wide range of codes, reducing guesswork by an additional 75% over Segmented GRAND. To leverage that advantage for soft-output decoding, we derive an accurate soft-output (SO) equation for GSegGRAND by extending soft-output GRAND (SOGRAND) to incorporate constrained guessing. Applying this SO to turbo product decoding, GSegGRAND achieves up to 88% guesswork reduction, making it a promising candidate for low-latency decoding in future communication systems.
tldr: This paper presents a generalized segmented GRAND decoding algorithm that reduces guesswork for turbo product decoding.
motivation: Existing segmented GRAND has limitations in the number of constraints and applicable code classes, motivating a more general approach.
method: The authors introduce a novel parity check structure and a transformation to map codes into this structure, enabling up to log2(n) constraints, and derive a soft-output equation for constrained guessing.
result: GSegGRAND achieves up to 75% additional guesswork reduction over Segmented GRAND, and up to 88% reduction in turbo product decoding.
conclusion: GSegGRAND is a promising low-latency decoding candidate for future communication systems.

title: Residual-Certified Adaptive Tracking Of Solution Manifolds In Parametric Dynamical Systems
authors: Yiran Xing, Yuandi Xu, Sulei Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a residual-certified adaptive method for tracking local solution manifolds in parametric dynamical systems. The method combines local POD reduction, full physical residual checks, state-distance snapshot forgetting, high-fidelity resampling, and a lightweight physics-informed neural correction. Instead of learning one global parameter-to-state map, the algorithm maintains the currently active local branch and updates it when the residual indicates loss of validity. The analysis explains why residual thresholds are meaningful on regular branches through local residual-error control, and why stricter local updates are needed near folds or other degenerate neighborhoods. Numerical studies on Ostwald ripening, a particle population-balance model, and the Bratu equation test the approach across low-dimensional dynamics, nonlinear nonlocal residual compensation, and near-fold model failure. The results show that residual-certified local model management can concentrate high-fidelity computation in difficult parameter regions while preserving an interpretable link between surrogate prediction, physical consistency, and active-branch tracking.
tldr: A residual-certified adaptive method for tracking solution manifolds in parametric dynamical systems using POD reduction and neural correction.
motivation: To efficiently track solution manifolds in parametric dynamical systems by adaptively updating local reduced-order models based on residual checks.
method: Combines local POD reduction, full physical residual checks, state-distance snapshot forgetting, high-fidelity resampling, and a lightweight physics-informed neural correction.
result: Demonstrates that residual-certified local model management concentrates high-fidelity computation in difficult parameter regions while preserving interpretability.
conclusion: The method provides an interpretable link between surrogate prediction, physical consistency, and active-branch tracking for parametric dynamical systems.

title: ETH-Hardness Of Learning Monotone Circuits And Approximating Their Size
authors: Bruno Cavalar, Susanna F. de Rezende, Matthew Gray, Rahul Santhanam
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the following hardness results for monotone learning and approximation of monotone circuit size: 1. Under the Randomised Exponential-Time Hypothesis (rETH), it requires time [MATH] to PAC-learn monotone formulas with [MATH] input bits and size [MATH] by monotone circuits of size [MATH], for every [MATH]. 2. Under the Randomised Exponential-Time Hypothesis (rETH), for any [MATH], there is a polynomially bounded function [MATH] such that [MATH]-multiplicatively approximating the minimum monotone circuit size of a monotone function consistent with a sequence of [MATH] labelled examples [MATH] over [MATH]-bit inputs requires time [MATH]. Our results are shown by a novel application of lifting arguments in proof and communication complexity to hardness of monotone learning, by building on the seminal result of Atserias and M\"uller (J. ACM, 2020) on hardness of automating Resolution proofs.
tldr: This paper proves hardness results for learning monotone circuits and approximating their size under the Randomized Exponential-Time Hypothesis.
motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of learning and approximating circuit size is fundamental to computational learning theory and complexity theory.
method: The authors use lifting arguments from proof and communication complexity, building on prior work by Atserias and Müller on automating Resolution proofs.
result: They show that PAC-learning monotone formulas by monotone circuits requires exponential time under rETH, and that multiplicatively approximating minimum monotone circuit size from examples is also hard.
conclusion: These results establish strong lower bounds for monotone learning and approximation, highlighting inherent difficulty in these tasks.

title: Near-Optimal Learning Of Gaussian Sobolev Operators
authors: Ben Adcock, Michael Griebel, Gregor Maier
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11921v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A key question in operator learning is how to design surrogate operators with provable approximation guarantees in reasonable computational time. Whereas smooth operators can be approximated efficiently, i.e., with at least algebraic convergence in the amount of training data, learning finitely regular operators is known to be less efficient. The reason is an intrinsic curse of sample complexity, which allows only subalgebraic sample complexity rates. This fact makes it all the more important to develop algorithms which provably achieve these rates. In this work, we present a fully data-driven algorithm, termed Hermite-PCA approximation, for learning Gaussian Sobolev operators with near-optimal sample complexity. It employs principal component analysis and weighted least-squares methods and is therefore computationally efficient. Moreover, it is spectral, in the sense that it achieves faster (and near-optimal) convergence the higher the Sobolev regularity. We provide a full error analysis of this algorithm, taking into account all sources of error, along with numerical experiments that verify our theoretical results and empirically confirm the efficacy of Hermite-PCA approximation for learning Sobolev operators.
tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven algorithm for learning Gaussian Sobolev operators with near-optimal sample complexity, focusing on operator learning theory rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Operator learning often suffers from curse of sample complexity for finitely regular operators; the authors aim to develop an algorithm that provably achieves optimal rates.
method: The Hermite-PCA approximation combines principal component analysis with weighted least-squares to learn Gaussian Sobolev operators in a spectral manner.
result: The algorithm achieves near-optimal sample complexity and faster convergence for higher Sobolev regularity, with full error analysis and numerical verification.
conclusion: Hermite-PCA approximation is an efficient, fully data-driven method for learning Sobolev operators, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Selective Avoidance Of Multiple Line-of-sight Obstacles At 130~m Using Locally Bending Space-time Wave Packets
authors: Layton A. Hall, Murat Yessenov, Isabelle Lebron, Ayman F. Abouraddy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-accelerating optical beams follow curved trajectories rather than propagating rectilinearly, which raises the prospect for avoiding line-of-sight (LoS) obstacles blocking the beam path. However, if a conventional laser beam is intercepted by an obstacle en route to an intended LoS target, then replacing this beam with a bending beam is not adequate: the obstacle is avoided but the target cannot be concomitantly reached. Rather, a laser beam that bends around the obstacle -- before continuing along its rectilinear path -- is needed. Here we show that engineering the spatiotemporal spectrum of a pulsed beam yields a space-time wave packet whose propagation dynamics can be tuned at will to locally bend around one or multiple obstacles, thereby avoiding them, to selectively reach a designated target. We carry out our experiments over distances extending to 130~m from the source, carried out in an open-air environment. In one scenario, the beam is incident on a target placed between two LoS obstacles, one preceding it and one following it -- both of which are avoided. In a second scenario, the locally bending beam avoids one and then two LoS obstacles preceding the intended target. These results may contribute to applications requiring selective incidence on targets in remote sensing, stand-off detection, directed energy, for optical and radio-frequency communications in presence of LoS obstacles, and for selectively delivered radiation therapies.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical wave packets that locally bend around obstacles to reach a target, using spatiotemporal spectrum engineering.
motivation: To enable laser beams to avoid line-of-sight obstacles while still reaching a designated target, which is not possible with conventional self-accelerating beams.
method: The authors engineer the spatiotemporal spectrum of a pulsed beam to create space-time wave packets with tunable propagation dynamics that locally bend around obstacles.
result: They experimentally demonstrate selective avoidance of one or two obstacles over 130 m in an open-air environment, reaching a target placed between or behind obstacles.
conclusion: This technique may benefit applications in remote sensing, communications, directed energy, and radiation therapies where selective incidence on targets is needed.

title: Haar Measure On Fuzzy Lie Group
authors: M. E. Egwe S. S. Sangodele
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a locally compact Lie group and \(d\mu\) a Haar measure defined on [MATH]. We consider the existence of a fuzzy analogue of [MATH] denoted by [MATH] called a fuzzy Lie group and develop a fuzzy Haar measure \(\mu_f\) on [MATH]. Also we construct a fuzzy Haar integral with respect to the corresponding fuzzy Haar measure on [MATH]. And finally we show that there exists a fuzzy Haar integral that is unique up to a multiplicative constant.
tldr: This paper develops a fuzzy Haar measure and integral on fuzzy Lie groups, extending classical Haar measure theory to fuzzy structures.
motivation: To generalize the concept of Haar measure to fuzzy Lie groups, enabling integration on fuzzy topological groups.
method: The authors define a fuzzy Lie group as a fuzzy set on a locally compact Lie group and construct a fuzzy Haar measure by fuzzifying the invariance properties of the classical Haar measure.
result: They show the existence of a fuzzy Haar measure and a corresponding fuzzy Haar integral, which is unique up to a multiplicative constant.
conclusion: Fuzzy Haar measure and integral provide a consistent framework for analysis on fuzzy Lie groups, analogous to the classical case.

title: Self-Referential Tests
authors: Siyona Agarwal, Julian Bernhoft, Karam Gill, Yonis Gulleth, Eric Huang, Benjamin Li, Brandon Ni, Soham Samanta, Leone Seidel, Boya Yun, Tanya Khovanova
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study self-referential multiple-choice tests with the question: The answer choices are positive integers. A value [MATH] is called if it occurs exactly [MATH] times among answer choices. The of a test is the sum of all answer choices, linking the problem to integer partitions. Using this framework, we define solvable and [MATH]-solvable tests and derive generating functions that enumerate them by cost, number of distinct valid values, and number of options. We also investigate extremal questions, including minimum costs and the maximum possible number of valid values. The paper was inspired by a puzzle from .
tldr: The paper studies self-referential multiple-choice tests where answer choices are positive integers, linking the problem to integer partitions and deriving generating functions for solvable tests.
motivation: The work is inspired by a puzzle and aims to formalize self-referential tests mathematically.
method: The authors define solvable and k-solvable tests, derive generating functions to enumerate tests by cost, number of distinct valid values, and number of options, and investigate extremal questions.
result: Generating functions are derived, and minimum costs and maximum number of valid values are explored.
conclusion: The paper provides a combinatorial framework for self-referential tests but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Approximate Monotonicity, Subadditivity, And Convexity In Weighted Topologies
authors: Angshuman R. Goswami
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The central question of this paper is the following: "If a topological space equipped with a weight function satisfies a certain property only approximately, can we recover the original structure without significantly altering the weights?'' To each open set of a topological space, we assign a non-negative weight and study approximate versions of three natural properties: monotonicity, subadditivity, and convexity. Through this study, we develop Hyers--Ulam-type stability results in general topology. In addition, we investigate several topology-specific cases, as well as present minorant and sandwich-type results.
tldr: This paper studies approximate monotonicity, subadditivity, and convexity in weighted topological spaces, developing Hyers-Ulam-type stability results.
motivation: The authors aim to understand whether topological properties that hold only approximately can be used to recover the exact structure without significantly altering weights.
method: They assign non-negative weights to open sets and analyze approximate versions of monotonicity, subadditivity, and convexity, using Hyers-Ulam stability theory.
result: They obtain stability results for these properties in general topology and explore specific topological cases, including minorant and sandwich-type results.
conclusion: The work extends Hyers-Ulam stability to weighted topological spaces, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Revisiting Simultaneous Methods For Dynamic Optimization In The Gpu Era
authors: Sungho Shin Joseph W. Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the classical topic in dynamic optimization: sequential vs simultaneous methods for solving DAE-constrained optimization problems, with a particular focus on how graphics processing unit (GPU) computing changes their effectiveness. Sequential methods offer key advantages through adaptive time stepping at the differential-algebraic equation (DAE) solver level, which is especially effective for handling stiff systems. However, long-time-horizon simulations remain a computational bottleneck, as time integration is inherently sequential and limits parallelization within the optimization algorithm. In contrast, simultaneous approaches are well-suited for parallel computing. They address these limitations by exploiting the highly repetitive structure of discretized DAE systems at the function evaluation level and leveraging sparse linear algebra routines that enable elimination tree-level parallelism. Although simultaneous methods typically lack adaptive time stepping, this limitation can often be mitigated by choosing a sufficiently fine initial mesh or iteratively adjusting mesh coarseness in an outer loop. In this work, we revisit the capabilities of the simultaneous approach in a GPU computing environment and assess its performance against a sequential method baseline. We employ a simultaneous approach based on orthogonal collocation within an open-source modeling framework and apply it to parameter estimation benchmarks from systems biology. We evaluate both GPU and CPU solvers on the simultaneous formulation. Our results show that, although less reliable, the simultaneous approach achieves up to 5.4x speedup compared to the sequential baseline among the largest instances where both methods solve successfully. The advantage of the simultaneous method with respect to problem size is more pronounced on GPUs than on CPUs.
tldr: This paper compares sequential and simultaneous methods for DAE-constrained optimization, leveraging GPU computing for speedup.
motivation: Dynamic optimization problems are computationally expensive, and the advent of GPU computing may shift the trade-off between sequential and simultaneous methods.
method: The authors implement a simultaneous approach using orthogonal collocation in an open-source framework and benchmark it against a sequential method on parameter estimation problems from systems biology, using both GPU and CPU solvers.
result: The simultaneous method achieves up to 5.4x speedup over the sequential baseline on the largest instances, with the advantage more pronounced on GPUs.
conclusion: Simultaneous methods are promising for large-scale dynamic optimization on GPUs, though they may be less reliable than sequential methods.

title: Contour-count Indicator Fields For Visible Pole Clusters In Meromorphic Continuation
authors: Xiaomei Yang Zhiliang Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a contour-count indicator method for visible pole clusters in outward meromorphic continuation from circular boundary data. The method starts from determinant characteristics built from positive Fourier coefficients. In the pure finite-pole model, the correct determinant characteristic factors into a polynomial whose zeros are the reciprocals of the exterior poles. In the presence of a holomorphic background, finite sampling, and noise, roots of individual determinants are unstable and are used only as local evidence. We aggregate this evidence into a scalar indicator field on the reciprocal pole plane: at each sampling point, the field records the fraction of determinant orders and shifts for which a small contour centered at that point encloses exactly one empirical determinant zero. The resulting field plays the role of a sampling-type imaging functional for pole visibility. Fixed superlevel sets give visible-pole clusters, while zero-dimensional persistent homology is used only as a threshold-robust post-processing step. We prove deterministic results linking pure-pole contour counts, Rouch\'e stability, indicator-field contrast, fixed-threshold component recovery, and persistence-gap stability. These results explain why isolated poles with sufficient residue and separation generate stable high-value components, whereas weak, close, boundary-near, or noise-dominated poles may give low, short-lived, or merged components. The framework is a cluster-certification and imaging method, not an unconditional all-pole recovery procedure.
tldr: This paper develops a contour-count indicator method for detecting visible pole clusters in meromorphic continuation from circular boundary data.
motivation: To provide a robust method for identifying pole clusters in meromorphic continuation when data is noisy or has a holomorphic background.
method: The method uses determinant characteristics from Fourier coefficients, aggregates local evidence into a scalar indicator field on the reciprocal pole plane, and applies fixed superlevel sets and persistent homology for post-processing.
result: Deterministic results link pure-pole contour counts, Rouché stability, indicator-field contrast, and persistence-gap stability, showing that isolated poles with sufficient residue and separation yield stable high-value components.
conclusion: The framework serves as a cluster-certification and imaging method, not an unconditional all-pole recovery procedure.

title: Diffusive Method For Multiple Class Data Classification
authors: Toyohiko Aiki, Honoka Yano, Takeshi Ohtsuka
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A simple algorithm for multiple class data classification is proposed, which is based on the infinit speed of propagation and the strong maximum principle for the heat equation. In this method, solutions of the heat equation whose initial data are the characteristic function of the training dataset are considered. The classification is established by the sign of the difference of two solutions in a very short time interval. A numerical algorithm for discrete training data in high-dimensional feature space is proposed. As an application of the proposed method, numerical results on the classification of handwritten digits database are presented in this paper.
tldr: This paper proposes a classification algorithm based on the heat equation, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a simple and efficient method for multiple class data classification using properties of the heat equation.
method: The algorithm uses solutions of the heat equation with initial data as characteristic functions of training data, and classifies based on the sign of the difference of two solutions over a short time interval.
result: Numerical results on handwritten digit classification are presented, demonstrating the method's applicability.
conclusion: The proposed diffusive method offers a novel approach to classification but is not connected to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Twisted Associative Algebras And Intertwining Operators
authors: Shun Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a vertex algebra [MATH] with a finite-order automorphism [MATH] satisfying [MATH] for some [MATH], we construct an associative algebra [MATH] and prove that the category of [MATH]-graded [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-coordinated [MATH]-modules is isomorphic to the category of graded [MATH]-modules. Furthermore, when [MATH] is a vertex operator algebra, we construct associative algebras [MATH] and [MATH], and establish that the categories of admissible [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-modules and ordinary [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-modules are isomorphic to the categories of graded [MATH]-modules and graded [MATH]-modules, respectively. By proving that [MATH] is isomorphic to [MATH], we obtain the equivalence between the category of [MATH]-graded [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-coordinated [MATH]-modules and the category of admissible [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-modules. Let [MATH] be three commuting automorphisms of [MATH] of finite order such that [MATH] and [MATH] for [MATH] and some [MATH]. Suppose that [MATH] is a [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-module for each [MATH]. We then construct an [MATH]-[MATH]-bimodule [MATH], and prove that the space of intertwining operators of type [MATH] is isomorphic to [MATH].
tldr: This paper constructs associative algebras for vertex algebras with finite-order automorphisms and establishes equivalences between categories of twisted modules.
motivation: To understand the structure of twisted modules for vertex algebras and their intertwining operators, which is a purely algebraic problem.
method: The paper uses algebraic constructions of associative algebras from vertex algebras with automorphisms and proves category equivalences.
result: It shows that categories of twisted modules are isomorphic to categories of modules over certain associative algebras, and that spaces of intertwining operators are isomorphic to bimodules.
conclusion: The work provides a unified algebraic framework for twisted modules and intertwining operators in vertex algebra theory.

title: Cross-Cutting Security Analysis Of LLM-Generated Code Via Metamorphic Testing And Association Rule Mining
authors: Zedong Peng, Chenggang Wang, Shangyue Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently generate code with security vulnerabilities, yet these weaknesses are rarely isolated: they often span multiple concern areas simultaneously, reflecting the cross-cutting nature of security in software. We present a framework that combines security-oriented Metamorphic Relations (MRs) with Association Rule (AR) mining to detect vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code, uncover their co-violation structure, and trace that structure back to prompt-level risk factors. We define nine MRs covering major CWE categories, including SQL injection, XSS, command injection, path traversal, hard-coded credentials, weak cryptography, and memory-safety errors, and apply them using an LLM-based judge to 3,700 code snippets generated by five open models from the LLMSecEval benchmark. The results show that 68.8% of snippets violate at least one MR, with hard-coded credentials (79.1%) and command injection (74.4%) among the most prevalent applicable failures. AR mining reveals strong cross-cutting co-violation patterns, notably that XSS and weak cryptography co-violations predict hard-coded credentials with 82.5% confidence (lift = 3.23), along with tightly coupled clusters linking authentication, credential handling, and cryptographic weakness, as well as input-handling and memory-safety failures. We then perform prompt-level risk analysis and find that database- and authentication-related prompts are strong predictors of broad cross-cutting insecurity, while 65.5% of prompts yield consistent violation outcomes across all five models. These findings show that insecure code generation is not merely a collection of independent defects, but a structured and prompt-conditioned phenomenon, motivating cluster-aware verification and prompt-level intervention for safer LLM-assisted programming.
tldr: This paper analyzes security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code using metamorphic testing and association rule mining.
motivation: LLMs often generate code with security vulnerabilities that are cross-cutting and not isolated, requiring a systematic analysis method.
method: The authors define nine metamorphic relations covering major CWE categories, apply them to 3,700 code snippets from five LLMs using an LLM-based judge, and mine association rules to find co-violation patterns.
result: 68.8% of snippets violate at least one MR; strong cross-cutting patterns are found, e.g., XSS and weak cryptography predict hard-coded credentials with 82.5% confidence.
conclusion: Insecure code generation is a structured, prompt-conditioned phenomenon, motivating cluster-aware verification and prompt-level intervention.

title: Rzk: A Proof Assistant For Synthetic $\infty$-Categories
authors: Nikolai Kudasov, Violetta Sim, Benedikt Ahrens
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Homotopy type theory (HoTT) is a type theory that allows for synthetic reasoning about [MATH]-groupoids. Several proof assistants (such as Rocq and Agda) implement variants of HoTT. Directed type theory is a type theory for synthetic reasoning about [MATH]-categories, where morphisms (or paths) of dimension 1 are not necessarily invertible. Among the proposals for directed type theory, the most developed is Riehl and Shulman's simplicial type theory (RSTT), based on simplicial shapes such as directed intervals and triangles. We present Rzk, a proof assistant implementing (a refinement of) RSTT for synthetic reasoning about [MATH]-categories. Specifically, the type theory implemented by Rzk is a computational variant of RSTT adjusted to make type checking practical. We define a translation from RSTT to Rzk and prove that it is sensible: every RSTT proof translates to an Rzk proof (faithfulness), and Rzk proves nothing new about RSTT types (conservativity). We also give a tutorial introduction to proving in Rzk, and describe its implementation, including the type-checking algorithm and the automated prover for the logic of shapes.
tldr: This paper presents Rzk, a proof assistant for synthetic ∞-categories based on directed type theory.
motivation: To enable synthetic reasoning about ∞-categories, which are fundamental in higher category theory and homotopy type theory.
method: Implements a computational variant of Riehl and Shulman's simplicial type theory, with a translation from RSTT to Rzk and a type-checking algorithm.
result: Provides a faithful and conservative translation, a tutorial, and an implementation with an automated prover for the logic of shapes.
conclusion: Rzk is a practical tool for formalizing synthetic ∞-category theory, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: $\mathrm{P}^{3}$CDA: Privacy-Preserving And Provably Secure Cross Domain Authentication Scheme For Internet Of Drones
authors: Chengqi Hou, Beibei Li, Ziqing Zhu, Yang You, Licheng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid expansion of the Internet of Drones (IoD) and the increasing mobility of drones, cross-domain interactions among geographically distributed domains have become inevitable. Cross-domain authentication is therefore a fundamental security requirement for IoD. However, existing authentication schemes often struggle to simultaneously achieve strong security, high efficiency, and identity privacy, making them unsuitable for the stringent requirements of highly dynamic and resource-constrained IoD environments. To address this challenge, we propose [MATH]CDA, a privacy-preserving and provably secure cross-domain authentication scheme. First, we design an efficient pseudonym management mechanism that supports adaptive pseudonym generation as well as batch registration, verification, and revocation. Second, we propose a structurally enhanced Merkle Hash Tree (MHT) that supports batch pseudonym updates, thereby reducing the pseudonym storage overhead of drones. Building on these components, we develop a cryptographic accumulator-based cross-domain authentication protocol that enables anonymous authentication with authorized pseudonyms while preserving the traceability and efficient revocation of malicious drones. We rigorously analyze the security of [MATH]CDA and formally prove its security under the Canetti--Krawczyk (CK) adversary model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that [MATH]CDA achieves lower computational, communication, and storage overhead than state-of-the-art schemes.
tldr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving cross-domain authentication scheme for the Internet of Drones using cryptographic accumulators and Merkle Hash Trees.
motivation: Existing authentication schemes for Internet of Drones fail to simultaneously achieve strong security, high efficiency, and identity privacy in highly dynamic and resource-constrained environments.
method: The scheme combines a pseudonym management mechanism with batch operations, a structurally enhanced Merkle Hash Tree for batch pseudonym updates, and a cryptographic accumulator-based cross-domain authentication protocol.
result: Security is formally proven under the CK adversary model, and experiments show lower computational, communication, and storage overhead compared to state-of-the-art schemes.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a practical and secure solution for cross-domain authentication in IoD, balancing privacy, efficiency, and security.

title: Open-Source Intelligence And Music Information Retrieval For Geographic Attribution Of Musical Affect And The Ecological Limits Of Population Inference
authors: Mohammadreza Rashidi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A common intuition holds that a region's music mirrors the temperament of its people, so that melancholic melodies mark melancholic populations. We test the measurable half of that intuition and reject the inferential half. Using the Essen Folksong Collection, a corpus of thousands of notated folk melodies, we extract real melodic and affect-related features from 2393 deduplicated melodies spanning 16 countries and 7 geographic regions, with the analysis performed on symbolic scores rather than audio. The mode of each melody is computed with a key-finding algorithm rather than read from the file, because the collection's own documentation warns its major and minor labels are unreliable. Cross-country differences in melodic structure are large and highly significant. All 8 tested features differ across countries at p<0.001, with the leap-related features reaching p<10^-90, and China carries a distinctive wide-leap, high-activity signature (arousal composite +1.24 standard deviations, mean absolute interval 2.77 semitones against Germany's 2.17). We then test the inferential half. We correlate the regional musical-affect measures with two published, validated national indices, the World Happiness Report ladder score and the Hofstede individualism index. None of the 6 correlations is significant (0 of 6). The geography of musical affect is real and measurable, but it does not predict how happy or how individualist a population is, and any claim that it does is an ecological fallacy. We release the full extraction and analysis pipeline, and a fail-closed checker re-derives every number in this paper from the data.
tldr: This paper uses music information retrieval to analyze folk melodies and finds that while musical features vary across countries, they do not correlate with national happiness or individualism indices.
motivation: The study tests the common intuition that a region's music reflects the temperament of its people, specifically whether melancholic melodies indicate melancholic populations.
method: The authors extract melodic and affect-related features from the Essen Folksong Collection, compute modes using a key-finding algorithm, and correlate regional musical-affect measures with the World Happiness Report ladder score and Hofstede individualism index.
result: All eight melodic features differ significantly across countries, but none of the six correlations with national indices are significant.
conclusion: The geography of musical affect is real and measurable, but it does not predict population-level happiness or individualism, and any such claim is an ecological fallacy.

title: FM-Receiver: A Foundation Model Enabled Unified Inner And Outer Neural Receiver Towards AI-Native Wireless Communications
authors: Tianyue Zheng, Chao Jiang, Linglong Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, neural receivers, which apply AI to improve wireless receivers have been developed. However, most existing neural receivers apply deep learning only to the outer receiver while retaining conventional channel decoding for the inner receiver, which prevents joint optimization and makes it difficult to build efficient and unified AI-native receivers. To address this issue, we propose a foundation model (FM)-enabled unified neural receiver, FM-Receiver, that integrates the outer and inner receivers into a single AI-native framework, by leveraging the strong representation capability of FMs. Specifically, we introduce a grouped error correction code Transformer that performs symbol-level channel decoding, enabling seamless integration of the inner and outer receiver. Building on this, we illustrate the proposed FM-Receiver, that directly takes the received signals as input of FM and outputs the recovered transmitted bits. In addition, a three-stage configuration-adaptive pre-training strategy is designed to improve the generalization ability to diverse system configurations and scenarios. Extensive simulations show that the proposed FM-Receiver achieves better performance than baselines across different system configurations. It also demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization to unseen frequency bands and scenarios.
tldr: This paper proposes a foundation model-based neural receiver that unifies inner and outer receiver processing for AI-native wireless communications.
motivation: Existing neural receivers apply deep learning only to the outer receiver, preventing joint optimization and efficient AI-native receivers.
method: The authors introduce a grouped error correction code Transformer for symbol-level channel decoding and a three-stage configuration-adaptive pre-training strategy.
result: The proposed FM-Receiver achieves better performance than baselines across different system configurations and demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization.
conclusion: The FM-Receiver provides a unified AI-native framework for wireless receivers, improving performance and generalization.

title: Auditable And Transparent Fully Authenticated Disk Encryption Via Usb Storage Interposition
authors: Gorka Guardiola M\'uzquiz Enrique Soriano-Salvador
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full Disk Encryption (FDE) has become increasingly important in the last decades due to the evident confidentiality concerns. In most systems, encryption is provided by an operating system driver, through which the user can transparently access the encrypted disk after supplying the required keys (or the credentials from which those keys are derived). In this work, we explore an alternative approach: the use of an intermediate USB device placed between the host system and the external hard disk, where the encrypted data are stored. Although there are existing devices that follow this inline approach (such as RAID controllers and USB enclosures with built-in encryption), we explore the use of a general-purpose single-board computer running Linux with USB On-The-Go support (e.g. a Raspberry Pi), to provide FADE (Fully Authenticated Disk Encryption). Our system, named CC (Cryptographic Companion), performs the cryptographic operations (encryption/decryption and authentication), providing a standard USB mass-storage interface to the host (which is entirely unaware of the presence of encryption) while relying on the external USB hard disk to store the corresponding encrypted blocks. Our design provides several key advantages: flexibility, low cost, transparency, the use of generic hardware and free and open-source software, adaptability to emerging cryptographic schemes, and mitigations against malicious disk firmware. This paper presents the design and implementation of the CC and an experimental evaluation of our current research prototype, which indicates that it is sufficiently efficient for most common use cases.
tldr: This paper presents a USB-based inline full disk encryption system using a Raspberry Pi, focusing on transparency, flexibility, and open-source design.
motivation: To provide an auditable and transparent full disk encryption solution that mitigates risks from malicious disk firmware and proprietary encryption hardware.
method: The authors implement a Cryptographic Companion (CC) using a Raspberry Pi running Linux with USB OTG, which sits between the host and the encrypted disk, performing encryption/decryption and authentication transparently.
result: The prototype is sufficiently efficient for most common use cases, offering flexibility, low cost, and adaptability to new cryptographic schemes.
conclusion: The CC approach is a viable alternative to OS-based FDE, with advantages in transparency and security against firmware attacks.

title: Expansion Of The Planetary Hamiltonian For Small Eccentricities And Inclinations: A Vector Formalism
authors: Federico Mogavero
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the classical expansion of the planetary Hamiltonian for small eccentricities and mutual inclinations of the orbits, presenting a derivation based entirely on vector formalism. We demonstrate that the secular part of the disturbing function, as well as any other Fourier harmonic, can be expressed in terms of scalar products of vectors lying in the system's invariant plane. Furthermore, we show how to express any such term using the angular momentum and eccentricity vectors of the orbits.
tldr: This paper presents a vector formalism for expanding the planetary Hamiltonian for small eccentricities and inclinations, focusing on celestial mechanics.
motivation: The classical expansion of the planetary Hamiltonian is important for studying planetary dynamics, and a vector formalism can simplify the derivation and expression of terms.
method: The author derives the secular part and Fourier harmonics of the disturbing function using scalar products of vectors in the invariant plane, expressing terms via angular momentum and eccentricity vectors.
result: The paper shows that the disturbing function can be expressed entirely in terms of scalar products of vectors, providing a compact and elegant formulation.
conclusion: The vector formalism offers a clear and efficient way to handle the planetary Hamiltonian expansion, which may be useful for celestial mechanics applications.

title: Cortet: Robust Generation Of Simulation-ready Cortical Meshes
authors: Davood Shahsavari, Irina Grigorescu, Jiaxin Xiao, Nashira Baena, Aakash Saboo, Vanessa Kyriakopoulou, Alena Uus, Martin J. Bishop, Katherine R. Long, Emma C. Robinson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every human brain folds differently, and such natural variation confounds the search for imaging biomarkers of neurodevelopmental disorders. Physics-based simulation can help determine the causal mechanisms that underpin this variability. Yet every simulation must be initiated from a solid tetrahedral mesh of the brain's interior, and it is the worst element in that mesh, not the average, that decides whether the simulation runs at all. Building that mesh from fetal MRI currently requires labour-intensive manual intervention. We therefore present CORTET (CORtical TETrahedral meshing): a fully automated pipeline that converts a triangulated cortical surface into a solver-ready tetrahedral mesh whose worst-element quality meets a strict stability target with no manual repair. By benchmarking against a general-purpose tetrahedral mesher on the same input surfaces, we isolate the pipeline's contribution from that of the input geometry, and we validate quality across a cohort of nearly 200 fetal subjects spanning the folding period. A mesh taken straight from the pipeline sustains a numerically stable morphoelastic folding simulation of a real fetal subject.
tldr: A fully automated pipeline for generating high-quality tetrahedral meshes of fetal brains from MRI for physics-based folding simulations.
motivation: Manual mesh generation is labor-intensive and error-prone, hindering large-scale studies of brain folding variability.
method: CORTET pipeline converts triangulated cortical surfaces into tetrahedral meshes with strict quality targets, benchmarked against general-purpose meshers on nearly 200 fetal subjects.
result: The pipeline produces solver-ready meshes that sustain numerically stable morphoelastic folding simulations without manual repair.
conclusion: CORTET enables automated, robust mesh generation for brain simulation, facilitating research into neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Defect Assignment Of The Clock Site In $^{229}\text{Th:CaF}_2$
authors: Daniel A. Rehn, Harry W. T. Morgan, Harris E. Mason, H. B. Tran Tan, Ricky Elwell, Igor M. Savukov, Michael J. Martin, Andrei Derevianko, Eric R. Hudson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of solid-state [MATH] nuclear clocks depends sensitively on the microscopic environment of the thorium nucleus in the host crystal. Here we reassess the dominant quadrupole-split thorium site in [MATH], which has been assigned to a thorium dimer in recent spectroscopic work. Thermodynamic estimates, density functional theory calculations, and electric-field-gradient comparisons instead favor an isolated [MATH] substitution on a [MATH] site charge-compensated by two nearby fluorine interstitials in a relaxed [MATH] motif. The same calculation identifies a higher-energy mixed-shell interstitial motif as a plausible minor site. The clock-active quadrupole-split site is therefore controlled by local fluoride compensation rather than unavoidable thorium aggregation. This defect assignment also has implications for achievable linewidths and provides a microscopic basis for reducing broadening in solid-state nuclear clocks.
tldr: This paper reassigns the dominant quadrupole-split thorium site in 229Th:CaF2 to an isolated Th4+ substitution with fluorine interstitial compensation, rather than a thorium dimer.
motivation: The performance of solid-state nuclear clocks depends on the microscopic environment of the thorium nucleus; correct defect assignment is crucial for understanding achievable linewidths and reducing broadening.
method: The authors use thermodynamic estimates, density functional theory calculations, and electric-field-gradient comparisons to evaluate candidate defect configurations.
result: The dominant site is an isolated Th4+ substitution on a Ca2+ site charge-compensated by two nearby fluorine interstitials, with a higher-energy mixed-shell interstitial motif as a plausible minor site.
conclusion: The clock-active quadrupole-split site is controlled by local fluoride compensation rather than thorium aggregation, providing a microscopic basis for reducing broadening in solid-state nuclear clocks.

title: Asymptotic Forms Of The Ursell Edge Waves On A Gently Sloping Beach
authors: P. Zhevandrov, A. Merzon, M. I. Romero Rodr\'iguez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that the asymptotics of the Ursell trapping modes on a sloping beach of small slope angle alpha coincide with the inverse Fourier transform of standard WKB exponentials, i.e., the Maslov canonical operator, as alpha tends to 0.
tldr: This paper studies asymptotic forms of Ursell edge waves on a gently sloping beach using WKB methods and Maslov canonical operator.
motivation: To understand the asymptotics of trapping modes on a sloping beach as the slope angle tends to zero.
method: The authors show that the asymptotics coincide with the inverse Fourier transform of standard WKB exponentials, i.e., the Maslov canonical operator.
result: The asymptotics of Ursell trapping modes are derived in the limit of small slope angle.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical connection between Ursell modes and WKB/Maslov theory.

title: Deterministic Minimum-Leakage Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Phase-Conjugated Twin Beams
authors: Dawei Wang Zhenlin Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimum-leakage continuous-variable quantum key distribution suppresses Eve's Holevo information by engineering the signal ensemble at the state-preparation stage. Existing symmetric minimum-leakage protocols achieve this goal by heralding: Alice interferes two squeezed ensembles, measures one output mode, and sends the other to Bob. Here we propose a deterministic two-mode protocol that removes the Alice-side heralding step. Alice combines two oppositely squeezed Gaussian ensembles on a balanced beam splitter and transmits both output modes, which form phase-conjugated twin beams. We show that this protocol is related to the heralding protocol through a common entanglement-based source but corresponds to a different prepare-and-measure decomposition. In the very-large-squeezing limit, the two protocols give the same secret key rate per transmitted optical mode. For finite squeezing, however, the phase-conjugated twin-beam protocol requires approximately 3 dB less squeezing to achieve the same key rate. We further analyze correlated two-mode Gaussian attacks in which Eve injects ancillary modes with optimized inter-mode correlations. We find that the correlated attacks are slightly more efficient than independent attacks, but the advantage remains limited under the minimum-leakage condition. These results show that phase-conjugated twin beams provide a deterministic and experimentally appealing route to symmetric minimum-leakage CV-QKD.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Counting Connected And Disconnected Ways To Assemble A Jigsaw Puzzle
authors: Prarthana Agrawal, Abdurrahman Hadi Erturk, Ard A. Louis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A jigsaw puzzle may be assembled in many different ways. Some assembly sequences remain connected throughout, while others temporarily build separate parts of the puzzle before joining them together. By representing the puzzle as a graph, these assembly sequences become vertex orderings that can be counted using recent results from graph theory. We apply this framework to enumerate three natural assembly strategies: connected assembly, assembly beginning from several disconnected pieces, and assembly in which new disconnected sections may be started during the process. The resulting counts reveal that, even for modest puzzle sizes, connectivity-preserving assembly sequences are greatly outnumbered by those that pass through disconnected intermediate stages.
tldr: This paper uses graph theory to count assembly sequences of jigsaw puzzles, comparing connected and disconnected strategies.
motivation: Understanding the combinatorial complexity of assembly processes, which may have implications for self-assembly or manufacturing.
method: Representing the puzzle as a graph and applying graph-theoretic counting of vertex orderings for three assembly strategies.
result: For modest puzzle sizes, connected assembly sequences are vastly outnumbered by those that pass through disconnected intermediate stages.
conclusion: Disconnected assembly strategies are combinatorially dominant, suggesting that natural or engineered assembly processes may often involve temporary disconnected components.

title: Analytical Evaluation Of Ramanujan Series For $1/\pi$ Via Degree-2, Degree-3, Degree-7 And Degree-19 Modular Equations
authors: Pablo Fern\'andez Refolio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an explicit analytical evaluation of Ramanujan-type series for [MATH]. Focusing on the singular moduli [MATH],[MATH],[MATH],[MATH] and [MATH]. We demonstrate that the underlying elliptic identities can be established through lower-degree modular equations; specifically, we resolve the cases [MATH] utilizing the modular equation of degree 2, the case [MATH] via a combination of degree-2 and degree-3 modular equations, the case [MATH] via a combination of degree-2 and degree-7 modular equations and the case [MATH] via a combination of degree-2 and degree-19 modular equations. In the first part of this work, we confine our attention to hypergeometric theory and elliptic integrals. Subsequently, in the second part, we extend our framework to incorporate the theory of elliptic functions, which allows us to address the higher-complexity modular identities.
tldr: This paper analytically evaluates Ramanujan-type series for 1/π using modular equations of various degrees.
motivation: To provide explicit analytical evaluations of Ramanujan-type series for 1/π by establishing underlying elliptic identities through lower-degree modular equations.
method: The authors use hypergeometric theory and elliptic integrals in the first part, and extend to elliptic functions in the second part to handle higher-complexity modular identities.
result: They successfully evaluate series for singular moduli using degree-2, degree-3, degree-7, and degree-19 modular equations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that Ramanujan-type series can be evaluated analytically using lower-degree modular equations, contributing to the theory of elliptic functions and modular forms.

title: A Ramanujan Pell Elliptic K3 Surface And Primitive Five-Cube Near Misses
authors: K. Srinivasa Raghava
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a trace-16 Ramanujan--Pell family of primitive positive five-cube near misses \[ a_n^3+b_n^3+c_n^3+d_n^3+e_n^3=t_n^3+(-1)^{n+1}, \] obtained from a six-cube identity of quadratic forms and the negative Pell orbit generated by \(8+\). The six coefficient sequences have rational recurrence generating functions with common reciprocal denominator \[ R(q)=1-257q-257q^2+q^3=(1+q)(1-258q+q^2). \] The quadratic identity is derived from a conic source, explaining the constants, while the Pell mechanism accounts for both the alternating error term and the denominator. The same construction yields the Mordell curve \[ E_K:\ y^2=x^3-432K(u)^2,\qquad K(u)=(1-13u+26u^2)^3+(6+182u^2)^3. \] We prove that its minimal smooth projective model is an elliptic K3 surface with geometric fibre configuration \(6IV\); over \(\mathbb Q\), the singular-fibre divisor is supported at one degree-two and one degree-four closed point. The section induced by the displayed decomposition of \(K\) has canonical height \(4/3\). The torsion groups over \(\mathbb Q(u)\), \(\mathbb Q()(u)\), and \((u)\) are respectively \(0\), \(\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z\), and \(\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z\). Over \(\mathbb Q()(u)\), the complex multiplication orbit of the section gives an Eisenstein Mordell--Weil sublattice and a visible generated rank-16 sublattice of the geometric Neron--Severi group of discriminant \(-108\); no fullness or primitivity is claimed. We identify the remaining free Mordell--Weil problem with an explicit equivariant Hom module, exhibit an anti-symplectic reciprocal involution, and show that \(w^3=K(u)\) has a Fermat-cubic quotient. No modularity assertion is made for the recurrence functions.
tldr: This paper constructs a Ramanujan-Pell family of five-cube near misses and studies an associated elliptic K3 surface, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper is motivated by number theory and algebraic geometry, specifically the construction of Diophantine equations and elliptic surfaces.
method: The authors use quadratic forms, Pell equations, and rational recurrences to derive a family of five-cube near misses, then analyze the associated Mordell curve and its K3 surface model.
result: They obtain a trace-16 Ramanujan-Pell family with alternating error term, and prove that the minimal smooth projective model is an elliptic K3 surface with specific fibre configuration and torsion groups.
conclusion: The work contributes to the study of Diophantine equations and elliptic surfaces, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Boolean Walsh Eta Units And Eisenstein Bases For Squarefree Levels
authors: K. Srinivasa Raghava
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be squarefree and let [MATH] be its Boolean divisor cube. To each Boolean character [MATH] we attach the eta-quotient \[ R_T^{(M)}(\tau)=\prod_{d\mid M}\eta(d\tau)^{\chi_T(d)}, \qquad \chi_T(d)=(-1)^{|T\cap\supp(d)|}. \] At squarefree level, the finite Fourier transform on the divisor cube simultaneously diagonalizes the squarefree Ligozat cusp-order matrix, Fricke complementation, Atkin--Lehner action on cusp labels, and the constant-term map for logarithmic Eisenstein series. In particular, for [MATH], \[ \ord_{1/c}R_T^{(M)} =}{24}\chi_T(c), \qquad \Lambda_T^{(M)}= \prod_{p\in T}(p-1) \prod_{}(p+1), \] and the forms [MATH] form a Walsh basis of the Eisenstein subspace of [MATH]. The structural theorem also determines explicit Fricke constants, Atkin--Lehner eigenvalues, good-prime Hecke eigenvalues, local [MATH] triangular blocks, a simultaneous bad-prime eigenbasis, and the indices of two explicit principal cuspidal divisor sublattices inside the formal degree-zero cusp-divisor lattice. As an application we specialize to the Heegner prime product \[ N=2\cdot3\cdot7\cdot11\cdot19\cdot43\cdot67\cdot163. \] The first Boolean boundary gives the eta-normalized Heegner-coloured partition product, while the top Walsh character gives the M\"obius eta-unit identity \[ D\log R_{\mathcal P}^{(N)}(\tau)=40415760- \sum_{n\ge1}\sigma_1(n^\perp)q^n. \] The same application gives algebraic modular-unit relations for the reciprocal partition product and exact Fricke-fixed logarithmic derivative identities for [MATH], interpreted through the modular completion of [MATH] and through accelerated paired products.
tldr: This paper studies Boolean Walsh eta units and Eisenstein bases for squarefree levels in number theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to develop a structural theory for eta-quotients and Eisenstein series at squarefree levels using Boolean Fourier analysis on divisor cubes.
method: It defines eta-quotients indexed by Boolean characters on the divisor cube, computes their orders and Fourier transforms, and derives explicit formulas for Fricke constants, Atkin-Lehner eigenvalues, and Hecke eigenvalues.
result: The forms form a Walsh basis of the Eisenstein subspace, and explicit identities are given for a specific Heegner prime product, including a Möbius eta-unit identity.
conclusion: The work provides a complete algebraic description of the Eisenstein subspace at squarefree levels, with applications to modular units and partition products.

title: Generalized q-Morgan Voyce Polynomials
authors: Yuksel Soykan Bahad{\i}r Y{\i}lmaz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study introduces and investigates generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials and their specific cases, including the first and second kinds of q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials, q-Horadam-Morgan-Voyce polynomials, and Fibonacci-type q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials. The generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials are defined by the recurrence relation featuring the specific q-power q^{n-2} and a negative sign, formulated as M_{n}(x,q) = (x+1+q)M_{n-1}(x,q) - q^{n-2}M_{n-2}(x,q) for n >= 2. The generating functions and explicit expressions for these polynomials are established by utilizing the Fibonacci operator and the binomial theorem. Furthermore, the study extends these polynomials to negative indices and derives the corresponding explicit formulas. Summation formulas and determinantal presentations of the generalized polynomials and their special cases are also comprehensively provided. Finally, the q-Cassini's formula for the generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials is established through the definition of specific square matrices and their subsequent recurrence relations.
tldr: This paper introduces and studies generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials, a family of q-analog polynomials defined by a recurrence relation, and derives their generating functions, explicit expressions, and combinatorial properties.
motivation: The study aims to extend the theory of Morgan-Voyce polynomials to a q-analog setting, exploring their properties and connections to other polynomial families.
method: The authors define the polynomials via a recurrence relation involving q-powers, use the Fibonacci operator and binomial theorem to derive generating functions and explicit formulas, and employ matrix methods to obtain determinantal presentations and q-Cassini's formula.
result: The paper provides generating functions, explicit expressions, summation formulas, determinantal presentations, and q-Cassini's identity for the generalized q-Morgan-Voyce polynomials and their special cases.
conclusion: The work contributes to the combinatorial theory of q-polynomials but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Crack Growth Forecasting Via Conditional Denoising Diffusion Models For Phase-Field Fracture
authors: S. M. Mallikarjunaiah Jahnavi Krishna Koda
abstract: ArXiv:2607.11971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The accurate prediction of brittle crack initiation, propagation, and complex topological evolution remains computationally prohibitive when utilizing traditional high-fidelity phase-field finite element methods. To overcome these computational bottlenecks, a physics-informed conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) is proposed for the full-field spatiotemporal forecasting of fracture evolution across diverse loading regimes and energy decomposition methods. The generative architecture is conditioned on rolling historical damage states and explicitly derived kinematic proxies -- phase-field velocity and gradient magnitude -- ensuring temporal coherence without non-physical artifacts. The principal contribution is spatially-localized uncertainty quantification without modification to the trained model. Ensemble variance concentrates at crack branching junctions ([MATH] at Y-junction bifurcations; zero high-uncertainty pixels in four deterministic propagation cases), while the high-[MATH] tail identifies high-error predictions with 90\% precision -- an 18-fold improvement over random selection. One-step crack tip localization achieves sub-pixel accuracy (0.12 px mean error) across both held-out validation subsets (shear-star and tension-spect), confirming cross-regime generalization. In closed-loop autoregressive rollout over 50 steps, the DDPM maintains Dice = 0.929 [MATH] 0.010 while a deterministic U-Net collapses to Dice = 0.423 under error accumulation, a 2.2[MATH] gap that establishes the value of stochastic re-sampling for long-horizon stability. Per-step inference requires approximately 3.6 s on an H100 GPU, approximately 28[MATH] faster than the FEM reference and 1{,}000[MATH] slower than a deterministic U-Net a cost that buys the stochastic diversity enabling uncertainty quantification.
tldr: This paper uses a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model for forecasting brittle crack propagation in phase-field fracture, with uncertainty quantification.
motivation: Traditional high-fidelity phase-field finite element methods are computationally prohibitive for predicting crack evolution; a faster surrogate model with uncertainty quantification is needed.
method: A physics-informed conditional DDPM is trained on historical damage states and kinematic proxies (phase-field velocity and gradient magnitude) to forecast fracture fields; ensemble variance provides uncertainty estimates.
result: The DDPM achieves sub-pixel crack tip localization (0.12 px error), maintains Dice=0.929 over 50 autoregressive steps (vs. 0.423 for U-Net), and identifies high-error predictions with 90% precision.
conclusion: Stochastic generative models offer long-horizon stability and built-in uncertainty quantification for fracture forecasting, outperforming deterministic baselines.

title: The Maximal Volume Of Projections Of The Cross-polytope
authors: Grigory Ivanov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the conjectured sharp upper bound for the volume of an arbitrary lower-dimensional orthogonal projection of the regular cross-polytope. More generally, for every spanning family [MATH] we prove \[ \nolimits_{k} \{\pm v_1, \dots, \pm v_n\} \le {k!} ^n v_i\otimes v_i\right)}. \] After the natural normalization, equality holds precisely when the non-zero vectors form an orthonormal basis. We triangulate the boundary of the absolute convex hull, compare the determinant of every radial simplex with the Gaussian solid angle of its positive cone, and then use that the radial cones form a complete fan. As a consequence, the volume of the projection of [MATH] onto any [MATH]-dimensional subspace is at most [MATH], with equality only for coordinate subspaces.
tldr: This paper proves a sharp upper bound for the volume of orthogonal projections of the regular cross-polytope, a purely geometric result.
motivation: The paper addresses a conjecture in convex geometry about the maximal volume of projections of the cross-polytope, which is a fundamental object in geometry.
method: The proof uses triangulation of the boundary of the absolute convex hull, compares determinants of radial simplices with Gaussian solid angles, and leverages the fact that radial cones form a complete fan.
result: The authors prove the conjectured sharp upper bound for the volume of any lower-dimensional orthogonal projection of the regular cross-polytope, with equality only for coordinate subspaces.
conclusion: The result settles a geometric conjecture and provides a complete characterization of extremal projections.

title: Tangent-Space Multiscale Manifold Methods For Nonlinear Elliptic Problems
authors: Anna Persson Mats G. Larson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a tangent-space multiscale manifold method for nonlinear heterogeneous elliptic problems. The method represents the fine-scale solution by a nonlinear reconstruction of a coarse state. The ideal reconstruction eliminates fine scales through a constrained variational problem, and the computable reconstruction approximates this map by localized nonlinear patch solves blended with a partition of unity. Because the approximation set is a nonlinear manifold, the coarse equation is posed with tangent multiscale test functions. We also formulate a network-interpolated variant in which only the restricted patch outputs used by the partition-of-unity blend, together with their tangent actions, are approximated by local learned maps. For heterogeneous monotone nonlinear diffusion, we record the structural monotonicity, differentiability, patch-map regularity, and conditional perturbation estimates that separate the geometric stability mechanism from localization, residual, and optional learning defects. A rigorous a priori theory for the decay of the localization defect, and the resulting convergence rates in the coarse mesh size, is deferred to a separate analysis; here these defects are controlled conditionally and their decay is demonstrated numerically.
tldr: This paper introduces a tangent-space multiscale manifold method for solving nonlinear heterogeneous elliptic problems, focusing on numerical methods for PDEs.
motivation: To efficiently solve nonlinear heterogeneous elliptic problems by representing fine-scale solutions through nonlinear reconstructions of coarse states.
method: The method uses a constrained variational problem for ideal reconstruction and approximates it with localized nonlinear patch solves blended via partition of unity, with a network-interpolated variant for efficiency.
result: The paper provides structural monotonicity, differentiability, and perturbation estimates, and demonstrates numerically the decay of localization defects.
conclusion: The method offers a rigorous framework for multiscale nonlinear problems, with convergence analysis deferred to future work.

title: Exact Solutions To A Class Of Constrained Optimal Control Problems Via Lossless Convexification For Digital Control
authors: Vaibhav Upadhyay, Siddhartha Ganguly, Debasish Chatterjee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article establishes a new numerically viable technique for solving a class of constrained, nonconvex, continuous-time optimal control problems (OCPs) for linear systems that commonly arise in aerial and aerospace applications. The lossless convexification technique is employed to translate the original nonconvex OCP with annular control magnitude constraints into a convex problem, and then by finitely parametrizing the control space with piecewise constant functions, an efficient numerical approach is established that guarantees exact solutions while ensuring the satisfaction of an uncountable family of constraints over a compact time interval. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated on a spacecraft landing problem involving three degrees of freedom (DoF), underscoring its potential for real-world aerospace guidance and control tasks.
tldr: This paper presents a lossless convexification technique for solving constrained optimal control problems in aerospace applications.
motivation: Aerospace guidance and control tasks often involve nonconvex optimal control problems with annular control constraints, which are challenging to solve exactly and efficiently.
method: The authors employ lossless convexification to transform the nonconvex OCP into a convex problem, then parametrize the control space with piecewise constant functions to obtain an exact numerical solution.
result: The approach guarantees exact solutions while satisfying an uncountable family of constraints over a compact time interval, demonstrated on a 3-DOF spacecraft landing problem.
conclusion: The proposed method provides an efficient and exact numerical technique for a class of constrained optimal control problems relevant to aerospace guidance and control.

title: Body-fitted Tracking Of 2d Open Curves With A Level Set Based Mesh Evolution Method
authors: Charles Dapogny
abstract: ArXiv:2607.12116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article describes a novel numerical algorithm for tracking the motion of a collection of open curves in two space dimensions. The proposed strategy combines two complementary representations of these curves at each iteration of the evolution process: on the one hand, they are meshed explicitly, as a sub-collection of the entities of a mesh of the total computational domain. Concurrently, using a variant of the Level Set Method, they are captured implicitly as algebraic combinations of the negative, zero and positive subsets of two auxiliary scalar functions, defined on the whole ambient space. This coupling of representations allows to perform accurate geometric or mechanical computations on these curves, while leaving room for large evolution of their shape. After the description of its main numerical ingredients, several applications examples of this methodology are proposed, where it is used to simulate the motion of open physical discontinuities, such as a vortex sheet roll-up, and to optimize the shape of open-ended curves, e.g. with respect to their anisotropic length, with the aim to improve the trajectory of a laser acting on a powder bed in the context of additive manufacturing, or to reconstruct fracture sets.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical algorithm for tracking open curves in 2D using a hybrid explicit-implicit representation.
motivation: Tracking open curves with large deformations is challenging; existing methods either lack accuracy or cannot handle topological changes.
method: The method combines an explicit mesh representation of curves with a level set approach using two auxiliary scalar functions to capture curves implicitly.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on vortex sheet roll-up, shape optimization for additive manufacturing, and fracture set reconstruction.
